1.1.1.title: Non-text Content
1.1.1.sentence: Create a text alternative for visual and auditory content.
1.1.1.goal: Non-text information is available to more people.

2.4.4.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
2.4.4.sentence: Provide descriptive names or context for all links.
2.4.4.goal: Users understand what each link will do.

2.4.6.title: Headings and Labels
2.4.6.goal: A page's content is described in headings and labels.

4.1.2.title: Name, Role, Value
4.1.2.sentence: Give components correct names, roles, states, and values.
4.1.2.goal: People using assistive technology understand all components.

1.3.1.title: Info and Relationships
1.3.1.sentence: Use code to reinforce relationships and information conveyed through presentation.
1.3.1.goal: Information about content structure is available to more people.

1.3.2.title: Meaningful Sequence
1.3.2.sentence: Use code to preserve meaningful content order.
1.3.2.goal: The order of content can be understood by more people.

2.4.3.title: Focus Order
2.4.3.sentence: Elements receive focus in an order that preserves meaning.
2.4.3.goal: Keyboard users navigate content in a correct order.

2.4.2.title: Page Titled
2.4.2.sentence: Provide a descriptive page title using appropriate technology.
2.4.2.goal: Each web page has a meaningful title.

2.4.10.title: Section Headings
2.4.10.sentence: Where content is organized in sections, provide section headings.
2.4.10.goal: Users understand how content is organized in sections.

2.1.1.title: Keyboard
2.1.1.sentence: Ensure pointer actions have a keyboard equivalent.
2.1.1.goal: Everything can be done with a keyboard except freehand movements.

2.1.2.title: No Keyboard Trap
2.1.2.sentence: Ensure users always know how to navigate away from components.

2.4.7.title: Focus Visible
2.4.7.sentence: Ensure each item receiving focus has a visible indicator.
2.4.7.goal: Users know which element has keyboard focus.

1.4.1.title: Use of Color
1.4.1.sentence: Use information in addition to color, such as shape or text, to convey meaning.
1.4.1.goal: Color is not the only way of distinguishing information.

1.4.3.title: Contrast (Minimum)
1.4.3.sentence: Provide sufficient contrast between text and its background.
1.4.3.goal: Text can be seen by more people.

1.4.5.title: Images of Text
1.4.5.sentence: Use text instead of pictures of text.
1.4.5.goal: Users can adjust how text is presented.

1.4.11.title: Non-text Contrast
1.4.11.sentence: Ensure meaningful visual cues achieve 3:1 against the background.
1.4.11.goal: Important visual information meets the same minimum contrast required for larger text.

4.1.3.title: Status Messages
4.1.3.sentence: Let assistive technology notify users about status changes that don't take focus.
4.1.3.goal: Make users aware of important changes in content.

1.4.10.title: Reflow
1.4.10.sentence: Make lines of text reflow within the viewport.
1.4.10.goal: Content can be enlarged without increasing line length.

1.4.13.title: Content on Hover or Focus
1.4.13.sentence: If hover or focus causes content changes, ensure interaction is predictable.
1.4.13.goal: More users can perceive and dismiss non-persistent content.

3.3.1.title: Error Identification
3.3.1.goal: Users know an error exists and what is wrong.

3.3.2.title: Labels or Instructions
3.3.2.sentence: Provide labels or instructions for inputs.
3.3.2.goal: Users know what information to enter.

3.3.3.title: Error Suggestion
3.3.3.sentence: Where errors are detected, suggest known ways to correct them.
3.3.3.goal: Users get suggestions on how to resolve errors.

1.4.4.title: Resize Text
1.4.4.sentence: Ensure text can be doubled in size.

1.4.12.title: Text Spacing
1.4.12.sentence: Ensure content adapts to user-defined text settings.
1.4.12.goal: Users can adjust text spacing to make it easier to read.

2.2.1.title: Timing Adjustable
2.2.1.sentence: Let users turn off, adjust, or extend time limits.
2.2.1.goal: Users have enough time to read and use content.

2.2.2.title: Pause, Stop, Hide
2.2.2.sentence: Let users control content changes that occur in parallel with other content.
2.2.2.goal: Fewer users are distracted by content that updates or moves.

2.5.3.title: Label in Name
2.5.3.sentence: Where practical, make the control’s text label and name match.
2.5.3.goal: Speech-input users can operate controls by their visible labels.
